answer: Each trust edge decays exponentially, losing half its weight at each temporal half-life, so an identity must sustain reciprocal, honest service to retain influence. In the EigenTrust matrix, freshly spawned Sybil identities have almost no trusted incoming mass and therefore near-zero eigenvector centrality, making consensus thresholds unattainable. A crystal-clear record of service distinguishes real trust from the fable of fabricated reputation; deceptive ripple effects are further limited by temporal decay and reciprocity weighting.
